title: Three stars is the minimum for anything on a public page or in a notification
description:
**Decision (Ryan, 2026-11-12).** "Three stars is our minimum standard for including anything on any public page or notification. References, Posts, Articles, anything."

**The one rule.** An item may appear on a public page or in a notification only if its effective human rating is at or above the site's floor (default 3 stars). Nothing else qualifies it.
- Where the rating lives: a Reference keeps `starRating`, `starRatedAt`, `starRatedBy` (`reference_stars.py`, the `setReferenceStars` mutation; the newest rating wins; clearing removes who and when). A Story (Post, Article) keeps the same three fields on its Item, copied forward by `carry_item_stars` on every new version (`item_stars.py`).
- How it is aggregated: today one editor's rating is the whole rating. Every reader of quality already goes through `item_stars.effective_rating` (0 means unrated); `aggregate_rating` is the seam where a vote aggregate would go. The floor reads `effective_rating(...).stars` and nothing else, so when aggregation arrives the floor follows with no change.
- Unrated is 0 and never qualifies. A Cyclotron prediction or confidence (`confidence`, `predictedAcceptProbability`, the "recommended" status) is a model's guess, not a human rating, and never qualifies, however high.
- An editor accepting a Reference or publishing a Story without stars does NOT qualify it. The page of a published Story stays reachable by its address; it is just not listed, fed, searched or mailed anywhere until someone rates it. Rating a pending Reference already accepts it (existing behaviour), so the editor's one action is "rate it".
- The floor is a site setting (`quality.floor_stars` in the standard front end config, 1 to 5, default 3), not a number in code. A site may raise it; it can never go below 1, because unrated can never be included.
- Stars stay private (`assert_no_item_stars`, docs/home-page.md): the floor is applied where the stars are known (the home page export, the projection's story-stars read, the notification assembler), so public snapshots and pages carry only items that passed, never a star count.

**Too few items.** A list shows fewer. It never lowers the bar and never fills with unrated or AI-only items. A list with nothing that qualifies renders nothing at all (no heading, no empty box), as empty includes already do. A notification with nothing that qualifies is not made.

**What changes in code (unrated items currently still show).** One filter, applied once where each consumer's candidate set is built, not re-implemented per page:
- `src/papyrus_content/home_page/export.py` (and `incremental.py`), the public Reference snapshot: export only accepted References with `effective_rating >= floor`. The `recommended` status (pending, predicted by the Cyclotron) is unrated by definition, so it leaves the public snapshot, and `select="recommended"` in `projection/standard/home_page_blocks.py` has nothing to show; the Worth-watching card (docs/home-page-groups.md) and any block using `recommended` go with it. Decision for Ryan below.
- `src/papyrus_content/home_page/ordering.py`: the tiers "unrated" and "1 to 2 stars" can no longer reach a public page, so public ordering is rating then Cyclotron confidence among qualifying items only (newsroom lists keep every tier). Coordinate with PPY-85fdba, which extracts this module.
- `projection/standard/projector.py` (`_story_stars`, `SiteIndex.story_stars`) and `story_order.py` (`rank_entries` today returns the list unchanged when nothing is rated; that must become "nothing qualifies, nothing listed"): drop entries below the floor where the projector builds the entry set that listings, feeds, the sitemap, search and section pages all read.
- `projection/standard/includes.py` (`listing_entries`, `listing_groups`, `fallback`): a fallback may not reintroduce unrated Stories.
- `projection/standard/feeds.py` (`feed_selection`; RSS and Atom) and `sitemap.py` (the URL list): same entry set; below-floor pages are in neither.
- Findings and Videos pages: the `medium="video"` Reference blocks and Findings blocks go through the same Reference filter; Posts and Articles pages through the Story filter.
- Public search index (docs/reference-search.md): index only items that pass.
- `src/papyrus_content/newsletter/roundup.py` (`items_in_window`, today every published non-issue item) and the unified issue assembler: filter by the floor. `newsletter/alerts.py` and `publish_alerts.py` (alerts fire when a Story is published): an alert fires when an item first reaches the floor, once ever per item, not at publish, because a fresh Story is unrated.
- A rating change re-renders the pages that list the item through the existing rating-dependency path; no new scan.

**Rollout (no behaviour change until a site turns it on).** First a read-only report per site: how many items on each public surface would drop, by title, so editors can rate what should stay. Then the site's version bump turns the floor on, one site under test first (batch-site-bumps).

**Specification.**
```gherkin
Feature: Three stars is the minimum for anything public
  Scenario: Rated items qualify
    Given a Reference rated three stars and a Story rated four stars
    Then both can appear on the home page, their section pages, feeds, sitemap, search and notifications

  Scenario: Unrated items do not qualify
    Given a published Story nobody rated
    Then it is not on the home page, its section page, the RSS or Atom feeds, the sitemap or search
    And its page is still reachable by its address and nothing is unpublished

  Scenario: Low ratings do not qualify
    Given a Reference rated two stars
    Then it appears on no public page and in no notification

  Scenario: A prediction is not a rating
    Given an unrated Reference the Cyclotron is 95 percent sure about
    Then it does not appear on any public page, including the Worth-watching card and the recommended lists

  Scenario: Accepted without stars
    Given an editor accepted a Reference and never rated it
    Then it is not public until it is rated three stars or more

  Scenario: Too few items
    Given only two items on a site meet the floor
    Then the home page list shows those two and nothing is added to fill the space
    And a list with no qualifying item renders no heading and no empty box

  Scenario: Every surface agrees
    Given an item at the floor
    Then it is on the home page, its section page, Findings or Videos by its medium, the feeds, the sitemap and search, all from one rule

  Scenario: Rated down
    Given an item on the home page rated four stars
    When an editor changes it to two stars
    Then the pages that list it are rebuilt without it and the feeds, sitemap and search drop it

  Scenario: Rated up
    Given an unrated Story
    When an editor rates it three stars
    Then it appears on the pages that list its kind and a published-story alert fires once

  Scenario: Notifications and the roundup
    Given a week with five published articles, two rated three stars or more
    Then the roundup draft contains those two and shows the other three as left out for not reaching the floor

  Scenario: A site raises the floor
    Given a site set to a floor of four
    Then three-star items disappear from its public pages and notifications, and other sites are unchanged

  Scenario: Stars stay private
    Then no public file carries a star count, only items that passed the floor

  Scenario: Aggregated ratings
    Given the rating of an item becomes an aggregate of several votes
    Then the floor reads the aggregate through the same function with no other change
```

**Impact (flag for Ryan): this drops content.** Today unrated items still show, and recommended (AI-predicted, unrated) References fill home page lists and cards. On anth.us and Machines on Machines, every unrated Reference, Post and Article, and every recommended Reference, leaves the home page, section pages, feeds, sitemap, search and the roundup the moment the floor is on. A site with few rated items will look nearly empty until editors rate. Hence the report first, the per-site switch second.

**Depends on:** none to build. **Blocks:** PPY-85fdba (ranking: the public tiers shrink) and PPY-849bf1 (roundup selection). **Related:** PPY-ba2f19 (stars shown), PPY-f24696, the no-prediction-no-show rule.

**Open questions for Ryan:** (1) An editor who accepts or publishes an item without stars: confirm it stays unlisted until rated (proposed), rather than counting as an implicit three. (2) Retire "recommended" (unrated, predicted) from every public page, including the Worth-watching card, or keep a clearly marked AI-only block outside this rule? Proposed: retire. (3) Rollout order: which site first, anth.us or Machines on Machines, after the report?
